# Join on 'city' as per operation history
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema: ['city', 'driver_count', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# Ensure types: city (string), driver_count (int), fare (float), ride_id (float)
# Convert driver_count to int (it should already be int, but enforce)
joined["driver_count"] = joined["driver_count"].astype(int)
joined["fare"] = joined["fare"].astype(float)
joined["ride_id"] = joined["ride_id"].astype(float)
joined["city"] = joined["city"].astype(str)

target = joined[["city", "driver_count", "fare", "ride_id"]]

# Write to target path without index
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' and 'driver_count' (both are non-float, leftmost columns in target schema)
# Aggregate 'fare' and 'ride_id' by mean to reduce duplicates and match target data scale
result = joined.groupby(["city", "driver_count"], as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean"
})

# Ensure column order and types match target schema
result = result[["city", "driver_count", "fare", "ride_id"]]
result["driver_count"] = result["driver_count"].astype(int)
result["fare"] = result["fare"].astype(float)
result["ride_id"] = result["ride_id"].astype(float)

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_63/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
